# The ROI Reckoning: Why Marketers Are Shifting from Demand Capture to Demand Generation


November 5, 2025 in[Blog](https://www.viantinc.com/insights/blog/)


Advertisers are waking up to what actually drives new business growth, which delivers improved return on investment ([ROI](https://www.viantinc.com/insights/blog/enhance-roi-and-dsp-advertising-efficiency-in-ctv/) ).


At this year’s[Association of National Advertisers (ANA)](https://www.ana.net/) Members-Only Conference in Irvine, California, Viant welcomed leaders from companies including Mazda, King’s Hawaiian, and Clorox to its headquarters to speak on one of the most important shifts in marketing today: understanding what truly drives ROI.


For years, the marketing mix has been heavily weighted toward channels like search, social, and retail media— places where consumers are often already signaling intent. These channels are powerful, measurable, and easy to optimize, but they’re often not where new customer acquisition actually begins.


When a consumer searches for a brand on Google or clicks a product ad on Facebook, they’re likely already in-market. They’ve seen something, heard something, felt something, oftentimes from a brand-building effort that happened earlier in the consumer journey, like a Connected TV ([CTV](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/omnichannel/connected-tv/) ) commercial, billboard, or an audio ad. Search, social and retail media may be where the conversion happens, but it’s rarely what sparked the interest in the first place.


That’s the fundamental difference between demand capture and demand generation, and it’s one that marketers are now being forced to confront.


## The 70/30 Problem


According to[eMarketer](https://www.emarketer.com/content/us-ad-spending-2024) , roughly 70% of all advertising budgets go toward search, social and retail media—channels that “capture” demand— and only 30% toward the other channels like CTV and streaming audio that create it.


“Performance marketing” looks great on paper: measurable, predictable, and trackable down to the click. But as Tim and Chris Vanderhook, Co-Founders of Viant Technology, explained in their keynote address at Viant’s event with the ANA in Irvine, performance marketing is really just demand capture, or harvesting intent that already exists.


“When a consumer searches for a branded term, the ad has already done its job,” Tim Vanderhook, Chief Executive Officer at Viant said. “Search is generally navigational. By the time someone types your name, they’ve already made their choice.”


That means many brands are spending the majority of their budgets buying back traffic from people who already know them, not securing new customers. As Jim Mollica, CMO of Bose aptly asked after evaluating the limited impact of branded search, “are we giving the cash register credit for the sale?”


And in the age of AI-driven search, that cycle is only getting more expensive. With Google’s AI Overviews crowding out organic and paid results alike, and[consumers turning to chatbots like ChatGPT or Perplexity for answers](https://tech.yahoo.com/ai/articles/study-reveals-people-ditching-google-090100369.html) , there’s no longer a guarantee that you can buy your way into visibility.


The only way in is if they ask for you by name.


## Reframing Performance and Brand Marketing


Marketers were challenged to reframe their thinking:


- Performance Marketing (Search, Social, Retail Media) = Demand Capture
- Brand Marketing (CTV, Streaming Audio, OOH) = Demand Generation


Demand Capture focuses on efficiency, squeezing incremental conversions from those already in the funnel. Demand Generation builds intent through the storytelling, visibility, and emotional connection that makes people want to enter the funnel in the first place. It builds baseline revenue and sustained growth that comes from recognition, trust, and recall.


Right now, most marketers have that mix backward. But Viant’s data shows the balance is starting to shift. “We’re seeing organizations go from that 70/30 split to something closer to 50/50,” Chris Vanderhook, Chief Operating Officer at Viant said. “They’re optimizing for growth, not just short-term ROI.”


## Incrementality: The Truth About What’s Working


When Viant runs[incrementality testing](https://www.viantinc.com/insights/blog/accurate-incrementality-testing-digital-advertising/) across channels in its Viant DSP, the results are striking.


In the Viant DSP, while CTV currently represents just 8-10% of total ad budgets, those same tests show CTV driving roughly 45% of incremental sales, meaning nearly *half* of new growth is coming from a channel that’s historically been underfunded.


As Chris noted, “Marketers are shifting more money into CTV and pulling it out of branded search, display, and social, because that’s where they’re seeing the impact.”


The key, he said, is to test everything:


“Does Meta have a place on your media plan? Of course. Does Google search have a place? Of course. But should they make up 70% of your budget? Of course not. You need to measure incrementality to understand the true value of each channel in your mix.”


## The Role of CTV in the New Mix


CTV is emerging as one of the most powerful tools for generating demand in a privacy-safe, measurable way. It blends the emotional and storytelling power of television ads with the precision and measurability of digital, giving brands the best of both worlds.


With Viant’s incrementality testing, marketers can now see how CTV drives new customers and growth, not just recycled clicks. CTV is finally performing like digital: measurable, efficient, and driving outcomes that matter.


## The Real Performance Play? Creating Demand That Lasts


The marketers who win in the next era won’t just capture demand—they’ll create it.


They’ll rebalance their budgets to build brand equity, not just chase attribution. They’ll test for incrementality to uncover what’s truly driving growth. And they’ll use transparent, measurable channels like CTV to reach audiences before they even start their search.


“It’s time to stop paying tolls to buy back the demand you already created,” Tim said. “Invest in creating new demand instead.”

## Frequently Asked Questions


What is a cookieless DSP?Expand


A cookieless DSP is a programmatic advertising platform that identifies and reaches audiences using durable, privacy-first identifiers rather than third-party cookies.


Instead of relying on fragile browser tracking, these platforms leverage advanced solutions like Household ID™ to maintain scale and precision. This approach ensures that digital campaigns remain effective and measurable regardless of evolving browser restrictions or privacy regulations.


How does programmatic advertising work without cookies?Expand


Programmatic advertising functions without cookies by activating first-party data through identity resolution frameworks like Unified ID 2.0 and the Household ID. Marketers also utilize contextual targeting to align ads with real-time content and prioritize natively cookieless channels such as CTV and DOOH. These methods allow for high-impact reach and frequency management without the need for invasive user-level tracking.


What is the difference between a DSP and a cookieless DSP?Expand


Traditional DSPs rely on syncing third-party cookies across exchanges to build audience profiles, a process that is increasingly fragmented and unreliable. A cookieless DSP uses people-based identity, first-party data, and privacy-safe signals to reach consumers across all devices.


Viant DSP was purpose-built to be cookieless from the ground up, ensuring it never relied on the legacy infrastructure of third-party cookies.


What targeting options are available in a cookieless environment?Expand


Marketers in a cookieless environment can utilize a robust suite of options including contextual targeting, first-party data onboarding, and household-level identity resolution.


Furthermore, interoperability with alternative ID frameworks like Unified ID 2.0 allows brands to maintain significant scale across the open web. These diverse tactics provide a durable, privacy-forward alternative to outdated cookie-based audience segments.


How is campaign performance measured in a cookieless world?Expand


In a cookieless world, campaign measurement is achieved through modern attribution models such as[incrementality testing](https://www.viantinc.com/insights/blog/incrementality-and-incrementality-testing-a-primer/) , Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), and secure data clean rooms.


The Household ID serves as a critical cross-device attribution layer, linking high-impact exposures on CTV to conversions on other digital devices within the home. This transition allows advertisers to prove ROI and optimize spend without relying on fragmented, cookie-based signals.
